issue.title: scan: treat error primitive as string

body:
@casualjim I think it's more complicated than that. Should it be explicit in a sense that it only adds stuff that are explicitly tagged with some `swagger:` mark-up, or should it be implicit, forcing users to explicitly mark types, attributes and methods when they want to exclude something? It seems to be something in the middle now :-(

Anyway, I sent PR #349 treating error as strings, I'm not sure if it's fine to change the fixture, please let me know what you think.

> Generating a spec for this file will yield: unknown primitive "actionParam"

I confirm. I found a similar error: unknown primitive "MyTypeName".

And this error is **random**.

I traced the error.

schemaParser.parseIdentProperty() call findSourceFile(), scan/schema.go, line about 690
findSourceFile (pkg \* loader.PackageInfo, typeName string), scan/schema.go, line about 760
This function not found information **sometimes**.

I traced next.

findSourceFile() called **with incorrect pkg parameter** sometimes. My package have name "myPackagePath/errors". It is similar golang system package name "errors". 

Sometime findSourceFile called with correct package name "myPackagePath/errors" and my correct typeName
Sometime findSourceFile() called with **incorrect package name "errors"** and my correct typeName

Under Linux (Ubuntu 14.04, 64-bit) and MacOS X (Yosemite) same. With Go 1.5.2, 1.6 - 64-bit
Under Windows 10, 64-bit - no errors. Or it is random? )))
wonderful, thanks so much for doing this

I was fool this bug.
I was rename my package "myPackagePath/errors" to "myPackagePath/apierrors".
go-swagger works fine after.

Problem is **random package names**. See my message above.

issue.title: Code generation changes depending on how swagger files are organized.
issue.body:
I have been trying to partition some definitions in different files and when I generate the code I noticed substantial differences between the single and multi files implementation. I attached the swagger sources. The single file is called single.yaml all the other ones belong to break up. The two things that change are:

The type Cell has an array of Resource in the single generation while it has an array of Resource\* in the multi generation.

The type VpcResource has a StringProperty\* in case of the single generation and a StringProperty in case of multi generation.

Issue 1 is definitely a problem.
